evals.prompt: I have observational survey data on remote-work adoption and job satisfaction, and I want to claim that remote work improves satisfaction. What design is this and can I make that claim?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-design-gate: identifies the data as observational/selection-on-observables, refuses to license a causal claim without a defended identifying assumption, and asks the user to name one (conditional ignorability / an IV / a DiD with parallel trends) or downgrade the claim to associational. Pins design_type + identifying_assumption in the Design Passport.

assertions.value: Routes to observational and requires a named, defensible identifying assumption before allowing any causal language.

evals.prompt: A minimum-wage increase took effect in one state in 2019 and I have employment data for many states before and after. How should I design this to estimate the effect on employment?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-design-gate and routes to difference-in-differences, naming PARALLEL TRENDS as the identifying assumption and telling the user to inspect pre-trends before estimating.

evals.prompt: Should my study of a new teaching method be an experiment or a quasi-experiment? I can't randomly assign students to methods.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-design-gate: because random assignment is impossible, routes away from a true experiment toward a quasi-experimental design (e.g. RDD if a cutoff exists, DiD if a rollout exists, or fixed effects), and pins the corresponding assumption; explains the credibility-for-information trade.

assertions.value: Distinguishes true experiment from quasi-experiment by whether the cause is randomly assigned, and names the QED assumption.

evals.prompt: A scholarship is awarded to students scoring above a test cutoff. I want to know if it raises graduation rates. What design fits?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-ssci-design-gate and routes to regression discontinuity, naming CONTINUITY at the cutoff (no score manipulation) as the assumption and suggesting a density/sorting check.

evals.prompt: My design is a two-group randomized experiment with a continuous outcome. Which statistical test should I run to compare the groups?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-test-selection-guard. The design is already fixed; choosing the specific statistical test (t-test vs Mann-Whitney) is downstream test selection, not design routing.

evals.prompt: I just want the mean and standard deviation of income in my sample, broken down by region — no design or causal question.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statistical-analysis for descriptive statistics. There is no design decision or causal claim to route here.
